chunks: Yūnus, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Fuḍayl, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “A father is not killed in retaliation for his child, but a child is killed in retaliation for his father; and a man does not inherit from another man if he kills him, even if it was by mistake.”
Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: We have already explained in the Book of Inheritances the manner of reconciling these two reports, so there is no point in repeating it.

key_terms.الْوَالِدُ: the father or parent in the legal ruling on retaliation
key_terms.الْوَلَدُ: the child in the ruling of retaliation
key_terms.بِوَلَدِهِ: for his child; indicating the parent-child legal relationship
key_terms.قَتَلَهُ: killed him; the act that prevents inheritance here

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on retaliation between a parent and child, and does a killer inherit from the victim in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning retaliation in cases of killing between parent and child, and it also states that the killer does not inherit from the one he killed, even if the killing was accidental. The closing note indicates that the reconciliation of related reports on inheritance was discussed elsewhere in detail.
